transcript.speaker: MAN
transcript.text: Sandra, I seem to remember you had some family visitors staying with you recently

transcript.speaker: WOMAN
transcript.text: Yeah that right. My brother and his family were here a couple of months ago.

transcript.speaker: MAN
transcript.text: OK, good. Well, I wanted to ask for your advice. I got my cousin and her family visiting next month and as I don’t have kids, I’ve no idea where to take them.

transcript.speaker: WOMAN
transcript.text: Right. What about accommodation? Are they going to stay with you in your flat?

transcript.speaker: MAN
transcript.text: No, thankfully. There wouldn’t be room. My cousin wants me to recommend a hotel. Do you know anywhere?

transcript.speaker: WOMAN
transcript.text: Yes, I do actually. I always recommend people stay at the King’s Hotel.
transcript.highlight_text: I always recommend people stay at the King’s Hotel.

transcript.speaker: MAN
transcript.text: Where’s that near?

transcript.speaker: WOMAN
transcript.text: It’s about a five minutes walk from Murray Station, so nice and central. It’s actually on George Street.

transcript.speaker: MAN
transcript.text: Oh yes, I know.

transcript.speaker: WOMAN
transcript.text: I think they’re on quite a tight budget, so how much roughly is it to stay there? If you book a family room, it’s about £125 per night. My brother paid for two double rooms in the end, and I think that was around £95 for each room.
transcript.highlight_text: If you book a family room, it’s about £125 per night.

transcript.speaker: MAN
transcript.text: Oh, that’s not too bad.

transcript.speaker: WOMAN
transcript.text: So how old are your cousins’ kids?

transcript.speaker: MAN
transcript.text: Twelve and nine. So I want to organise some trips while they’re here. I was thinking of doing a bus tour of the city centre, as none of them have been here before.

transcript.speaker: WOMAN
transcript.text: Those bus tours are quite expensive. I think it’s better to do a walking tour. It gives you a much better feel for the city. There’s one that starts from Colton Square. It takes a couple of hours and doesn’t cost that much.
transcript.highlight_text: I think it’s better to do a walking tour.

transcript.speaker: MAN
transcript.text: Sounds good. I’ll look that up. Thanks.

transcript.speaker: WOMAN
transcript.text: If the weather’s nice, one thing you could do is visit the old fort. You could get there by boat. The whole trip takes half a day.
transcript.highlight_text: You could get there by boat.

transcript.speaker: MAN
transcript.text: That’s a really good idea. I’d like to do that myself. And if the weather bad I was thinking they could go to the science museum. But maybe they could do that when I at work.

transcript.speaker: WOMAN
transcript.text: Yeah don forget it closed on Mondays

transcript.speaker: MAN
transcript.text: They here from Saturday for four nights so Tuesday would be best I think
transcript.highlight_text: so Tuesday would be best I think

transcript.speaker: WOMAN
transcript.text: And it won’t be so crowded then. Saturdays are terrible. I took my kids to the exhibition on old computers there and it was far too crowded. I wanted to go back but it’s finished now.

transcript.speaker: MAN
transcript.text: That’s a shame. My cousin’s kids would have enjoyed that.

transcript.speaker: WOMAN
transcript.text: There’s another one starting soon on space, which looks really good too.
transcript.highlight_text: There’s another one starting soon on space,

transcript.speaker: MAN
transcript.text: OK, well, I’ll mention that to my cousin.

transcript.speaker: WOMAN
transcript.text: Have you thought about where to take them to eat?

transcript.speaker: MAN
transcript.text: Well, I really like all the food stalls at Clacton Market. My cousin’s vegetarian. I know it’s one of the best places for that kind of food.

transcript.speaker: WOMAN
transcript.text: Definitely, and there’ll be loads of choices for the kids too. You need to get there quite early, though. At the weekend, most of the stores stop serving lunch at 2.30.
transcript.highlight_text: most of the stores stop serving lunch at 2.30.

transcript.speaker: MAN
transcript.text: Good point. It’s all going to need careful planning. My cousin said she’d love to take the kids to a show at the theatre, but tickets are so expensive.

transcript.speaker: WOMAN
transcript.text: I know. But you can get some good deals if you book online with bargained tickets for the following day. On some seats there a 75 discount
transcript.highlight_text: On some seats there a 75 discount

transcript.speaker: MAN
transcript.text: Really. I must try and get some

transcript.speaker: WOMAN
transcript.text: Yeah There are lots of things you can do for free as well. No need to spend a fortune.

transcript.speaker: MAN
transcript.text: Like what?

transcript.speaker: WOMAN
transcript.text: They’re coming next month, right? Well, check and see if it’s the same weekend as the Roots Music Festival in Blakewell Gardens.

transcript.speaker: MAN
transcript.text: R-O-O-T-S?

transcript.speaker: WOMAN
transcript.text: Yeah, check it out online. It’s always a family-friendly event and there’s no entry charge.

transcript.speaker: MAN
transcript.text: That sounds perfect.

transcript.speaker: WOMAN
transcript.text: And if you’re in Blakewell Gardens, climb Telegraph Hill. You’ll be able to look right down on the port. Everyone’s always really impressed because it’s so huge.
transcript.highlight_text: You’ll be able to look right down on the port.

transcript.speaker: MAN
transcript.text: Oh yeah, I’ve been meaning to do that for ages. I’ve heard the view’s amazing.

transcript.speaker: WOMAN
transcript.text: Yeah, it’s really worth the effort.

transcript.speaker: MAN
transcript.text: Well, that’s given me loads of ideas. Thanks so much.
